item.dc:creator: yogavida
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Our website address is: https://yogavidawellness.com.

What personal data we collect and why we collect it

Comments

When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Contact forms

Cookies

If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Analytics

Who we share your data with

How long we retain your data

If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

item.title: Philosophy
item.dc:creator: yogavida
item.content:encoded:
It is health that is real wealth, not pieces of gold and silver.

Mahatma Ghandi

About Shannel

Philosophy

Yoga is a Sanskrit word meaning 'to join' or 'union'. I like to think the practice of yoga unites an individual’s body, mind and soul, and prepares them to live life with awareness.

The practice of asanas (postures) is only one aspect of the Eight limbs of Yoga. The philosophy of Yoga Vida (Vida meaning ‘life’ in Spanish) is yoga is more than just an exercise or practice of postures. Our aim is to promote these eight steps that act as a guideline on how to live a purposeful and meaningful life. 

The practice of yoga works on our physical body increasing strength, flexibility and balance. But yoga can work deeper to cleanse and detoxify our organs, and improve function of the main systems of the body for example respiratory, digestive, endocrine. On a mental level, yoga can be calming as we take control of the minds endless chatter through correct breathing and meditation. Our concentration and focus improves and we can efficiently go about our daily lives which can be so demanding in this world we live in. 

My classes work on the energetic fields, the subtle part of us we cannot feel or touch. There are seven key points in the subtle body that are thought to be vortexes of energy, known as chakras. When energy becomes blocked in a chakra, it triggers physical, mental, or emotional imbalances that manifest in symptoms such as anxiety, lethargy, or poor digestion. I like to tap into these chakras freeing up the energy in the direction of where you want it to go. 

Yoga Nidra is fast becoming popular as it is one of the deepest forms of meditation. You experience stillness in a dreamless sleep whilst staying awake (yes hard to get your head around it!). We can access deep impressions that have formed and create new positive ones with affirmations and regular practice. 

So in the demanding fast-paced world we live in, these ancient teachings that have been handed down have proven to still hold value. More and more people are turning to holistic approaches such as yoga to help prevent and sometimes cure ailments, and to live a balanced and happy life. I hope yoga can help you in whatever way you need it.

item.title: Pregnancy Yoga
item.dc:creator: yogavida
item.content:encoded:
Take time to do what makes the soul happy

- Sadguru

get in touch

Pregnancy Yoga

In Ayurveda the pregnant woman is viewed as a precious and delicate creature who should be treated with honour and respect. It is important for her to be happy and healthy during this period of major change. Positive physical, energetic and emotional transformations will benefit both herself and her unborn child. Therefore, Yoga is ideal for pregnancy as its techniques of breath, movement, meditation and relaxation support these changes and help prepare for labour.

The key physical benefits of yoga are to enhance strength and fitness of the mother-to-be, keeping the body supple whilst toning the pelvic floor, hip and abdominal core muscles, in preparation for the birthing process. Balance, posture and stability improve to adjust to the gradual weight changes.

Yoga helps to boost energy and relieve stress and anxiety. It also promotes relaxation and restful sleep. Through breathing and visualisation techniques, the mother can nurture and nourishingly bond with her baby.

Preparations of the physical body and certain breathing techniques can also help relieve pain in labour and childbirth.

The benefits of Yoga do not end there. Common ailments during pregnancy can be relieved (e.g. swollen joints, heartburn, shortness of breath, constipation, nausea, headache, carpal tunnel syndrome).

Online

Saturday Mornings 9.30 - 10.45 am.

Join us online via Zoom for a gentle flow class suitable for pregnancy. This nourishing class incorporates fluid movement, deep breathing, alignment, balance, strength, flexibility and relaxation. Please state your pregnancy on the registration form when booking. You should also send a short message to Shannel here.

Online classes give you the flexibility to practice within the comfort of your own home. Whether your new to yoga or a seasoned practitioner, this class is for everyone. Shannel will be able to give you clear instructions, alignment cues and modifications.

Tickets :

  • Can be booked using class pass: Block of 5 Online Yoga Classes £40 (£8 per class)

Individual or Group Pregnancy sessions can be booked at a time that is convenient for you. Group sessions can include family, friends and corporate.

TRAINING AND QUALIFICATIONS

I trained in pregnancy yoga with Yoga Campus London, a Yoga Alliance UK accredited school. I was fortunate to have studied under the guidance of Uma Dinsmore-Tuli and Lisa White.

Uma, founder of Womb Yoga, leads retreats and courses worldwide, sharing the approach to Yoga Therapy set out in her CD's, DVD's and books; Mother's Breath, Teach Yourself Yoga for Pregnancy and Birth and Feel Confident: Yoga For Living and Yoni Shakti.

Lisa, owner of Yoga Place E2, holds the Birthright Perinatal Diploma, is BWY certified, and completed her own Teacher Training with Yoga Campus.

Mum And Baby Yoga

This is a great opportunity to ease yourself back into exercise after the birth of a baby. The postures and poses are specially designed to include your newborn in a relaxed and safe environment.

Benefits include restoring a sense of well-being for Mum through gentle exercise and breathing techniques. We work on strengthening and toning the muscles of the abdominals, pelvic floor and back. The relaxed atmosphere in our group classes allow mums a chance to de-stress as well as meet other mums in a social environment. 

For baby, the focus is stimulating healthy development and promoting better sleep and a more settled behaviour. This is a special time for parent and baby to bond and interact. Dads are also welcome of course!

Suitable after 6 weeks after birth (10 weeks after caesarean birth).

item.dc:creator: yogavida
item.content:encoded:

Children's Yoga

Our children live in a busy world of school pressures, homework, exams, after school activities, video games, internet, materialism and competition. At a young age they are already familiar with the word 'stress'. It is common for adults to turn to yoga to manage their own stress and help them relax. Many wish they had only found yoga earlier. Yoga for children can sow the seeds of a life-long practice that will continue to deepen. 

Physically, children's yoga enhances flexibility, strength, co-ordination and body awareness. Yoga poses stretch and strengthen muscles and through integrating breathing and movement, muscles become warm and flexible. 

Our world of digital technology makes unnatural postural demands on our little bodies. All that time hunched over tablets, laptops, phones etc. leaves young and old backs alike compressed, tight and sore. It is important our children's spines develop upright and lengthened. Yoga encourages this process resetting the spine to its natural shape.

Balancing poses teach children focus which increases concentration and attention naturally. Balancing skills promote a stillness and quietening of the mind. Following a sequence of poses teaches us how to move with ease, control and co-ordination. 

The practice of yoga encourages self-esteem, compassion and body awareness. Children learn how to honor and respect their bodies from a young age. We learn to respect others as we begin to understand we are all the same- built of the same stuff. We are just in different forms. 

Experiencing meditation and relaxation in classes, children can learn to relax, be at peace and how to navigate themselves through life's challenges with more ease. A deeper connection with their inner self and the natural world that surrounds them begins to develop. 

Importantly children have fun in yoga classes. From partner work to yoga games impersonating animals to feeling like a warrior, they connect with their inner child (as will all adults who give it a try). 

As a teacher i want to provide a loving, responsive, creative environment for children to discover their world and uncover their own truths. I believe yoga is a wonderful gift to help do just that. 

Yoga in schools - early development

In my classes, I try to incorporate educational themes as I am familiar with The Primary Curriculum and Statutory framework for the Early Years Foundation stage.

These themes can be taught alongside yoga postures, breathing exercises, meditation and relaxation, all of which promote healthy ways of living whilst teaching children spelling, numeracy etc, therefore making the classes educational all round. 

There are so many ways aspects of the Early Years Framework can expressed in yoga classes. Communication and language, physical, personal, social and emotional development, understanding the world we live in, arts and design as well as mathematical and literacy skills. 

Classes are supposed to be fun and interactive. We form letters and words using our bodies, learn a vast variety of child friendly yoga poses and then combine them into our yoga games and stories. We become creative with our own ideas and learn ways of expressing them.

We sometimes partner up and learn how to respect and understand others. And we accept our own limitations and learn more about dealing with emotions.

item.content:encoded:
"Rejuvenate in Kerala"

An Ayurvedic and Yoga Wellness Experience in India

Date: 21st to 28th November 2026
***Last remaining spaces***

Quick Navigation

Retreat Experience | Accommodation | Prices & Packages | Booking Form

FAQs | Terms & Conditions

Omesh & Shannel invite you to our Ayurvedic Yoga Retreat in Kerala, India.

Kerala, the homeland of Ayurveda, offers the perfect blend of tropical serenity, ancient healing traditions and soul-nourishing natural beauty, making it an ideal setting for deep rest, renewal and transformative wellbeing.

Our mission is to give you holistic rejuvenation through a variety of authentic Ayurvedic therapies, yoga, meditation, nourishing food and more. A chance to un-plug and re-charge, away from the hustle of your daily routine.

You will experience practices, tools and techniques that you can take with you after the retreat for your ongoing self-care, well-being and the greater good. And the chance to connect with like-minded, kindred spirits and make lasting friendships.

The Retreat Experience

Retreat Venue

The award-winning Manaltheeram Ayurveda Beach Village is set along the Malabar Coast at the southern tip of India, where palm-lined shores meet the waters of the Arabian Sea. The venue features a collection of traditional cottages and houses, dedicated Ayurvedic treatment rooms, a swimming pool, and peaceful spaces to relax and unwind throughout the day. Guests should fly into Thiruvananthapuram (TRV) Airport, where a private transfer to the resort will be arranged. The journey takes approximately 40 minutes.

Accommodation

Guests may choose to stay in rooms within the traditional houses, garden-view cottages, or sea-view cottages. Each space blends contemporary comfort with traditional architectural character, creating a peaceful and authentic environment for rest and restoration. All rooms are air-conditioned and Wi-Fi enabled, and are thoughtfully equipped to ensure a comfortable stay. Amenities include drinking water, fresh towels, daily newspapers, reception support, a fruit basket, hair dryer, tea-making facilities, bathroom essentials, in-room safe, slippers, mosquito nets, and access to ironing facilities.

Food

All meals are Ayurvedic, vegetarian, sattvic, and freshly prepared, designed to support digestion, balance, and overall wellbeing. The cuisine is gentle and not overly spiced, making it suitable for those new to Ayurvedic food as well as sensitive stomachs. You can expect a good variety of nourishing dishes, with some familiar elements appearing regularly throughout the retreat. This consistency is intentional in Ayurveda and supports the body’s natural rhythms, allowing the digestive system to rest and reset.

Treatments

Daily authentic and traditional Ayurvedic treatments are included as part of your retreat experience, with sessions lasting up to two hours and often performed by two therapists. A dedicated team of experienced Ayurvedic doctors and therapists will guide your journey, providing bespoke advice and personalised treatment plans following an individual consultation. All medicines and therapeutic products used are derived from organically grown medicinal plants, cultivated within the retreat gardens, ensuring purity, quality, and authenticity.

Yoga and Meditation

Each day you will be guided through morning and evening sessions, led by Omesh or Shannel. Classes are suitable for all levels and are thoughtfully designed to reflect our combined experience across a range of yoga traditions and philosophical teachings. Yoga is a holistic and spiritual discipline rooted in a subtle and ancient science, supporting harmony between body, mind, and breath. Meditation sessions invite you to turn inward, cultivating presence, clarity, and deeper awareness.

Book Now

We are excited to be collaborating with our rich backgrounds in yoga and holistic teachings. Allow us to share the magic and let us safely and lovingly guide you back home to yourself.

Your Hosts

Shannel is a multi-disciplined practitioner of Yoga and Wellness of over 15 years, her passion extending to Ayurveda as well as skills in both Chakra and Theta Healing.

She grew up in East Africa, lived in the UK and now resides in Dubai. She has traveled extensively including stints in South America, Southern Asia, Central Asia, Australia and Bali as part of her spiritual journey.

She deepened her practice of Yoga in India, where she studied and qualified across the key limbs of Hatha, Vinyasa Flow, Ashtanga, Yin and Restorative Yoga.

Shannel further qualified in the specialisms of Children’s, Pre & Post Natal, Women's Health Yoga as well as Guided Meditation.

Her life journey has brought her a profound exploration of spirituality, enriching her practice and teaching. The sudden loss of her father at a young age, coupled with other significant personal challenges, has deeply influenced Shannel's spiritual growth and dedication to wellness. These life experiences have fueled her passion for understanding the unique needs and strengths of individuals, particularly women, at different life stages. This passion drives her to create supportive and empowering wellness practices that foster both physical well-being and spiritual growth.

Omesh grew up in Jammu & Kashmir, India, adhering to the central theme of Sanatan Dharma, following the principle paths of yoga ie Bhakti, Jhana, Karma, and Raja Yoga, more as a way of life without being consciously aware of it.

From early childhood he was fortunate to be surrounded by highly spiritual people and exposed to their philosophy of life.  

Omesh had his first formal taste of yoga in 2006 when he was working in the corporate sector.  Although he worked his way up in that world, he always felt it wasn’t really what he wanted in life. He felt a strong connection to yoga, and it pulled him back into its sphere of influence when a close friend reintroduced him to yogic philosophy.

Although his studies in India adhered to the highest standards, he has lived in England for many years and understands that different cultures require modification of methods and techniques.

Omesh has been visiting India on a yearly basis, and over the years has attended many workshops organised by the Divine Life Society and the Swami Sivananda Foundation on Bhakti Yoga, Meditation and Ayurveda.

What's Included

  • 7 nights full-board accommodation (en-suite, AC, free wi-fi)
  • Airport transfers from Thiruvananthapuram International Airport (TRV)
  • Welcome gift bag
  • Daily yoga and meditation classes/workshops (for all levels) taught by Omesh and Shannel
  • One to one initial, daily and final consultation with an Ayurvedic doctor
  • Daily Ayurvedic treatment (lasting 90 mins to 2hrs a day)
  • Free Ayurvedic medicines during the treatment period
  • All meals freshly prepared with locally sourced, seasonal, Sattvic, vegetarian ingredients
  • Beach and pool access
  • Ayurvedic cookery class
  • Ayurveda herbal garden tour
  • Special Kerala cultural evening
  • Backwaters boat excursion to Poovar Island
  • Aazhimala Shiva Temple visit

What's not included

  • Flights and travel to Thiruvananthapuram International Airport
  • Visas for India
  • Travel and health insurance
  • Excursions and activities outside of our schedule
  • Additional treatments and medicines outside of our programme
  • One to one sessions

Accommodation

There are 5 room categories to choose from. All rooms are designed in a traditional style -simple, relaxed, and harmonious with nature: paths among coconut trees, green lawns, and a calm beachfront ambience

Standard Room

Simple rustic-style accommodation (≈ 18m²) designed in a natural, minimal-style bungalow or cottage format

Garden Cottage

Surrounded by tropical greenery, charming stand-alone cottages (≈ 20–25 m²) with garden views and a small terrace or veranda

Special & Deluxe Cottage

Traditional Kerala architecture meets comfort. Special cottages have a partial sea view and Deluxe cottages have a full sea view (≈ 22–25 m²), and often include a hammock or outdoor seating

Kerala House Deluxe

Quieter, secluded heritage style wooden houses (≈ 30 m²) with partial sea views through palms and greenery, and a terrace with chairs or a hammock.

Retreat Investment

Please select your preferred room category and indicate whether you would like single or shared occupancy. If you choose shared occupancy, you will have the opportunity to specify your preferred roommate.

Room availability is limited and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

All rooms can be arranged with either one large double bed or two single beds. Each room includes an en-suite bathroom, air-conditioning, and Wi-Fi for your comfort.

Reserve Your Space

Reserve Your Place

Thank you for your interest in joining us in Kerala.
Please complete the short booking request form below.
We will confirm availability and send you the deposit information within 48 hours.

Frequently Asked Questions

Here are a few common questions. If you need anything else, feel free to contact us.

Do I need prior yoga experience?

No previous yoga experience is required. All sessions are adaptable and suitable for beginners through to more experienced practitioners. You’ll be guided to practise at your own pace.

What kind of food will be served?

All meals are Ayurvedic, vegetarian, sattvic, nourishing, and freshly prepared to support healing and digestion. The cuisine is gentle and not overly spiced, making it suitable for sensitive stomachs and those new to Ayurvedic food.

Meals are designed with balance and consistency in mind, so you can expect a good variety of dishes, with some similar elements appearing regularly throughout the retreat. This repetition is intentional in Ayurveda and supports the body’s natural rhythms and digestive health.

Dietary requirements can usually be accommodated and will be collected via the registration form closer to the retreat.

What should I expect from the accommodation?

Accommodation at the retreat resort is best described as a comfortable 3-star standard, with a focus on cleanliness, functionality, and connection to nature rather than luxury finishes.

Rooms are simple, peaceful, and well-maintained, designed to support rest and the healing process. The value of the retreat lies in the holistic programme, Ayurvedic treatments, nourishing food, and immersive experience, rather than high-end hotel amenities.

How many people will be attending the retreat?

The retreat welcomes up to 25 guests, creating a supportive group environment with a strong sense of community. This size allows for shared experiences, connection, and group energy, while still ensuring guidance, care, and personal attention throughout the retreat.

Can I attend the retreat on my own?

Absolutely. Many of our guests join solo and quickly feel part of the group. The retreat is designed to be welcoming, inclusive, and supportive, offering plenty of opportunities for connection as well as space for personal reflection.

When will I receive the registration form?

The registration form will be sent approximately three months prior to the retreat start date. This timing allows you to share accurate information once your plans are in place.

The form will collect key details including:

  • Contact information
  • General health information (to support your wellbeing during the retreat)
  • Dietary requirements
  • Additional room or extra-night requests (subject to availability)
  • Travel details
  • Information relating to recommended immunisations and health guidance for travel to India
  • Guidance relating to visa requirements

This information helps us prepare your experience with care and ensure a smooth, supportive stay.

What is the payment schedule?

A £500 non-refundable deposit is required to secure your place. The remaining balance is due two months prior to the retreat start date. Payment details will be shared once your booking request is confirmed.

What time is check-in and check-out?

Check-in is at 12noon and check-out is at 10am.

Can I arrive early or stay an extra night?

Where availability allows, additional nights before or after the retreat may be possible. As early check-in and late check-out cannot be guaranteed, extra nights are offered closer to the retreat date, once flight details are confirmed.

Information about availability, rates, and how to request additional nights will be shared via the registration form sent approximately three months prior to the retreat. This helps us manage requests fairly and avoid unnecessary changes.

What should I pack?

A detailed packing list will be shared closer to the retreat, however as a guide we recommend bringing:

  • Lightweight, breathable yoga clothing
  • Comfortable walking shoes or sandals
  • Swimwear for the pool and beach
  • Loose, comfortable clothing for Ayurvedic treatments and relaxation
  • Casual, comfortable outfits for excursions
  • Relaxed, casual or dressy clothing for evening meals (upto you)
  • A light rainproof jacket or poncho (Kerala can be humid with occasional rain)
  • Sunscreen and a hat for sun protection
  • Mosquito repellent

You may also wish to bring a reusable water bottle, a light shawl or layer for early mornings or evenings, and any personal items that support your comfort and wellbeing.

This retreat has been created with deep care, intention, and respect for the Ayurvedic tradition. It is an invitation to slow down, to rest deeply, and to reconnect with yourself in a supportive and nourishing environment. If you’re feeling the call to pause and restore, we would love to welcome you to Kerala.

Shannel & Omesh, Retreat Leaders

Terms & Conditions

  • A non-refundable deposit payment of £500 will be required to reserve your space. Bank transfer payment details will be provided.
  • The remainder of payment will be due by 21st September 2026.
  • For any cancellations 60 days prior to the start of the retreat, a refund of payment minus reservation deposit will be issued.
  • For any cancellations within 60 days of the start of the retreat, no refund is possible as advance payment for your space will have been made to the venue.
  • In any circumstance where the host is required to cancel, and no alternative event is offered, you will receive a full refund of your investment.
